To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
urban regeneration initiatives need as a minimum to promote security and increase leisure opportunities in order to enhance quality life and mental health, and to improve the image of a locality.
urban regeneration initiatives need to be more than just a focus on jobs and houses.
urban regeneration is not sufficient to improve quality of life or to prevent the deterioration of mental health in deprived communities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the need for urban regeneration initiatives to address the quality of social relations, and the need for local residents to be actively engaged in the process of urban regeneration.
the need for urban initiatives to address more fundamental issues than those related to jobs and housing.
the need for more holistic approaches to urban regeneration which take into account the complex and dynamic nature of people’s perceptions of locality and how they cope with the effects of adversity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
urban regeneration initiatives have a limited role in enhancing quality of life and reducing social inequalities in mental health.
the regeneration initiative has not yet made a significant contribution to improving the mental health of local residents.
urban initiatives should aim to improve people’s perceptions of their local area, and to do so they need to take account of people’s perceptions of the locality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the urban regeneration initiative in this case was not sufficiently responsive to local needs.

The main takeaway from our work is that
in order to make an impact on the quality of life and/or mental health of local residents, the focus should be on the social aspects of the environment and the social capital of local communities.
urban regeneration initiatives should focus on the quality of life and social capital in the locality, and the impact of this on the lives of people vulnerable to mental illness.

urban regeneration is a long term process and that it is important to understand the perceptions of those living in the area, and to engage with them to ensure that their needs are met and that the process of urban regeneration does not further marginalise them.
